# NPM Improved v1.7.6

## NPMX heartbeat recovery and ACME reliability

- Fix secondary peer versions becoming permanently stale on the primary when snapshot sync is interrupted. Secondary nodes now send a lightweight authenticated heartbeat independently of the configuration snapshot process, approximately every 20 seconds when the NPMX primary is reachable.
- Distinguish stale/offline peer heartbeats (older than 90 seconds) from genuine version/protocol incompatibility. ACME coordination still fails closed when any paired secondary has not checked in or is incompatible; no validation attempts are sent to Let's Encrypt until the cluster is ready.
- Require the HMAC-authenticated sender identity to match an already-paired secondary before the primary accepts a heartbeat. Prevent signed requests from registering arbitrary node IDs or spoofing another peer.
- Surface failed NPMX status polling instead of silently returning, so unreachable primary / authentication errors can be diagnosed.

## Deployment

Update both the primary and secondary to v1.7.6. The secondary uses its existing configured primary URL and signed NPMX credentials; no re-pairing or database manipulation is expected. Confirm the primary shows a fresh heartbeat from the secondary before retrying certificates.

No certificate deletion or database migration is required. This corrects peer liveness reporting and does not by itself verify external port-80 forwarding.
